grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle 9 Conflict II cards and deal 5 above them; shuffle 3 Conflict I cards and deal 1 on top. This makes a face-down 10-card deck. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.

grades.reason: All three tiers are independently shuffled, the correct 4/5/1 cards and bottom-to-top order are given, and unused cards are returned unseen.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: Four-player human: start at 1 VP; three-player human: start at 0 VP. Both start with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their nearest garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup: “Score marker—on 1 for a four-player game, otherwise on 0”; “two Agents”; “three…garrison…remaining nine”; “Take 1 water.”

grades.reason: Both score starts, the two active and one reserved Agent, the 3/9 troop split and locations, and starting water are given.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain; after Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you (Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Reveal turn may be taken early; “Resolve Reveal Effects”; “Clean Up”

grades.reason: Early Reveal is permitted, subsequent turns are excluded, only just-revealed cards supply Reveal effects, and all played cards are discarded at Clean Up.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: No: entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving effects from the destination or the played Agent card, so those later resources cannot pay that entry. One card sends only one Agent, using one chosen Agent icon. A card without Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may be revealed.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn entry-cost timing; “You choose only one Agent icon”; “no Agent icons”

grades.reason: Entry precedes Agent-card and destination gains, one card sends one Agent, and a card without Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison: five total in this example. A non-Combat space does not permit normal deployment. Recruits come from your supply into your garrison; at a Combat space, recruited this turn may then deploy.
observed.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: “any or all units recruited during your current turn…plus up to two more”

grades.reason: The maximum is five: three current-turn recruits plus two older garrison troops; ordinary noncombat deployment is excluded and recruitment comes from personal supply. The key's empty-supply consequence is background to the origin question, rather than an additional requested scenario.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon permits sending an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where your Spy currently sits; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy for one card draw, chosen immediately after Agent placement and before any space/card effects. The same Spy cannot serve both abilities; two different Spies can serve Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but only one Gather Intelligence draw is allowed per placement.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: “Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access”; “Gather Intelligence”

grades.reason: Spy-icon access without recall, other-player Infiltration by recall, immediate pre-effect Gather Intelligence, and separate-Spy and single-draw limits are all distinguished.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2 + 1 sandworm × 3 + 4 swords = 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
observed.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; “if your last unit is ever removed”; Intrigue cards

grades.reason: The calculation gives eleven; losing the last unit gives zero strength, and no unit means no Combat Intrigue eligibility.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent acting again if an opponent later plays; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply (not garrison), Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
observed.evidence: Combat: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; cleanup

grades.reason: An earlier pass does not bar later action, consecutive passes close the window, and troops and sandworms have the correct supply/bank cleanup destinations. Strength adjustment and marker reset are key background not requested here; marker reset is separately asked in Q91.

observed.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. observed.evidence: Combat ties: “Exactly two tied first”; “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.”

grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; multiple worms do not multiply beyond doubling. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP, or pay the cost a second time (6 spice total) to gain 2 VP.
observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “one or more”; exceptions and optional reward example

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check for a match against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. In the Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, for the same 1 VP pair flip.
observed.evidence: Battle Icons: “must flip the matching pair”; Endgame wild match

grades.reason: The post-win supply check uses another face-up Conflict or Objective, matching is mandatory for one VP, and the Endgame wild may match any of the three icons.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP. Merely tying the Alliance holder does not steal it: you must rise above their Influence (or the separate FAQ holder-loses-Influence rule may transfer it).

grades.reason: The answer distinguishes reversible two-Influence VP, retained and repeatable four-Influence track bonus, and the Alliance with its associated VP; tying does not take it and a higher challenger does. Describing the Alliance and its VP together is accepted as contextual linkage of the VP to the token rather than an assertion of a permanent, separate VP.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

observed.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it across sources to buy one card or split one source across cards. After buying a Row card, refill the Row immediately and you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal timing, pooling/splitting, Row refill, discard pile

grades.reason: Reveal purchase interleaving, pooling and splitting, buying a replacement after refilling, and the face-up discard destination are all covered.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

observed.answer: A visit to a Maker space takes all bonus spice there. At Makers, an Agent-free space gets one additional spice during Makers phase. Deep Desert costs 3 water and Hagga Basin costs 1 water. Worm options require Maker Hooks; a protected Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin cannot receive a summoned worm while the Shield Wall remains. The usual sandworm icon may require Hooks if printed as a condition, but Hooks are not universally required; they are retained, not spent. A sandworm can never go in a garrison, and cannot be summoned at those three protected Conflicts until the Wall is removed.
observed.evidence: Sandworms; Makers; Board Space Guide; Shield Wall

grades.reason: Maker bonus collection and accumulation timing, Hooks when specified, and Shield Wall restrictions on Conflict summoning are explained, together with the prohibition on garrison placement. Its references to Conflicts receiving summoned worms, the protected-Conflict exception and the garrison prohibition communicate the legal Conflict destination in context. The question does not separately ask the bank origin or immediate timing.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: Endgame triggers at the end of a round if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue; then compare VP. Tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “At the end of a round”; Endgame Intrigue; tiebreakers

grades.reason: The trigger is at round end, Endgame Intrigues precede comparing VP, and all four resource tiebreakers are in order.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: With CHOAM, take one of the available face-up contracts on the board into your supply, then replace it face up from the bank if a bank contract remains. The printed icon guide gives 2 Solari if there are none left; this does not require every contract token in the game to have been acquired. In particular, another human with no public contract available gains 2 Solari even if Shaddam's set-aside Sardaukar contracts remain unacquired, and cannot take those reserved contracts. Without CHOAM the icon also gives 2 Solari. Shaddam's own reserved-contract option follows Sardaukar Commander and the FAQ. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified total spice during that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. observed.answer: With CHOAM, take a face-up public contract and refill its offer face up from the bank if possible; if none are face up, gain 2 Solari. Harvest completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the contract’s spice amount that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes when taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts

grades.reason: The public contract is taken and refilled when possible, no public offers gives two Solari, and Harvest, Immediate and next-acquisition completion triggers are correct. The answer states the ordinary public-offer fallback; it does not claim that reserved contracts are public or deny Shaddam his separate Leader option. Unasked reserved-contract details are not imported as extra question parts.

observed.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.

grades.reason: A newly acquired space contract cannot retroactively complete; completion is announced, rewards gained, and the token flipped down and retained in supply.

Turn order begins First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never Reveals.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

If Recall does not trigger Endgame, humans return Agents to Leaders; in 3–4 human play pass First Player clockwise, while in two-player play return Rival Agents to supply and pass First Player to the other human.

grades.reason: All five phases are in order, Conflict precedes the five-card hand, and Recall returns Agents and passes First Player with the two-player exception.

observed.evidence: Agent Turn: pay before effects; “may carry out all these effects in any order.”

If the placement effect specifies a required connected Agent-icon type, the Spy may be placed only at a post connected to that icon; otherwise placement is not legal.

grades.reason: A new Spy goes from supply to an unoccupied post, an exhausted personal supply may be replenished by a no-effect recall, and specified icon connections constrain placement.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?

Winning the corresponding Conflict places/replaces a Control marker. If the Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit. grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?

grades.reason: Tied second takes third without affecting the winner, tied third gets nothing, and three tied first each get second with no card or further reward.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separate from your deck; after resolving, discard them face up beside the Intrigue Deck. If its draw deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes an Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets steals one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

observed.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once when you acquire that card. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal and cannot carry over.

grades.reason: Acquire effects occur once on acquisition, empty-deck draw triggers reshuffling and continued drawing, and unused Persuasion is lost.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on Reveal turns remain in play until Clean Up (unless trashed first). Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate each other regardless of order played. Clean Up ends that in-play status by moving the cards to discard.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond

grades.reason: Agent and Reveal cards remain in play through Reveal resolution until Clean Up unless trashed, and two Bond cards can supply one another's other Fremen regardless of order.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1147–1157; FAQ p3 Retreat

observed.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; the recalled Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” may mean zero.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops

grades.reason: Recall excludes the newly placed Agent and permits a later turn that round; retreat returns troops to garrison and any number includes zero.

grades.question: When an effect grants two Influence with a freely chosen Faction, may it be split? What is required for an Alliance-icon effect or a minimum-Influence effect?
grades.expected: Choose one Faction, both Influence there (not split). Alliance effect requires holding shown Faction Alliance token; minimum-Influence effect requires at least shown value with shown Faction.

observed.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token. An effect with a minimum Influence requirement requires that level in the named Faction.

grades.reason: A single two-Influence effect cannot be split, and minimum-Influence and Alliance-icon effects require the corresponding threshold or token.

grades.question: If an Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, who receives the token? If the holder drops to 3 and no one has 4, what happens?
grades.expected: Former holder chooses one of previously tied opponents to receive token; holder loses Alliance VP and receiver gains it. Below 4 loses token; if no eligible 4+ player return token to board, losing its VP.

observed.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, and both remain tied, the former holder chooses which tied opponent receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its VP.

grades.reason: The former holder chooses among the previously tied opponents; falling below four without an eligible holder returns the token to the board and loses its VP. The first clause asks the recipient choice rather than separately requesting VP arithmetic on transfer; the second clause's token return and VP loss are explicit.

grades.question: What happens to a card drawn during Reveal compared with one drawn after Reveal? What happens to a Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal?
grades.expected: During Reveal immediately reveal and use this turn; after Reveal keep until next round, then draw five extra. Plot effect for later Reveal stays face up until that Reveal, use then discard.

observed.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and used this turn; a card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect remains face up until then, is used, then discarded.

grades.reason: During-Reveal draws are used immediately, after-Reveal draws are kept in addition to the next five cards, and delayed Plot cards remain face up until used and discarded.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?
grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.
grades.source_references: FAQ p4 When you win a Conflict

observed.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.

grades.reason: Tying first is not winning, while an appropriate win-trigger Intrigue received as a winning reward may be played immediately.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.
grades.source_references: FAQ p2 Endgame; p4 Victory Points

observed.answer: If VP and all listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12 spaces.

grades.reason: The most recent Reveal breaks a complete final tie, and scores may exceed twelve.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?
grades.expected: Completion mandatory; all same-space contracts completed with one Agent placement. Their effects may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; still must hold them at placement.

observed.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you cannot delay completion. Their effects are another effect of the Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, provided you held them when placing the Agent.

grades.reason: Held same-space contracts must all complete on the visit, and their effects may be ordered with other Agent-turn effects without waiving prior ownership.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.
grades.source_references: Main p17; FAQ p3 Shaddam Corrino IV

observed.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; only he may acquire them, choosing one instead of a public contract when acquiring a contract. His Signet restriction begins immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Reserved Sardaukar; Shaddam; FAQ Shaddam

grades.reason: The reserved contracts are not initially possessed, acquisition may substitute a reserved Sardaukar contract, and the deployment restriction is immediate and turn-only.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.
grades.source_references: Main p17 / extraction 957–964; FAQ p3 Reverend Mother Jessica

observed.answer: Feyd’s token begins on the leftmost space of the Training track; when it reaches the rightmost space, it stays there. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.

grades.reason: Feyd begins leftmost and stays at the rightmost end; Lady Jessica begins face up and Reverend Mother's ability is usable on the flip turn.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

observed.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2. Margot/Irulan may reach 2 with that Faction again later after losing Influence and regaining it; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.

grades.reason: Upward passage through two counts and may recur after losing Influence, downward passage does not, and Clean Up is not a hand discard for Spacing Guild's Favor.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade Agent icon: draw one card and resolve a contract icon; it does not automatically gain Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor Agent icon: gain one Emperor Influence and resolve a contract icon. Without CHOAM each contract icon gives 2 Solari. With CHOAM, take an available public face-up contract into your supply and refill from the bank if possible; the icon gives 2 Solari if no such contract remains. For another human, Shaddam's unacquired set-aside Sardaukar contracts are unavailable and do not prevent this fallback when the public supply is empty. Shaddam's reserved-contract acquisition option remains governed by his Leader and the FAQ.
grades.source_references: See benchmark-v17/source-reference-appendix.json: original main PDF pp16,20, Uprising Board Space Guide, original Shaddam Leader and official FAQ p3, exact named-file/hash locators.

observed.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access; it costs nothing, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM gain 2 Solari; with CHOAM take a public face-up contract and refill if possible, or gain 2 Solari if offers are exhausted. It gives no automatic Faction Influence and is not Combat. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, costs nothing, gains one Emperor Influence (counted once) and resolves the same contract icon; it is not Combat. It advances Emperor automatically, unlike Accept Contract.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide; human contract icon rule; Faction status

grades.reason: Both access icons and ordinary effects are right; the shared contract icon has its CHOAM and no-CHOAM branches, while only Dutiful Service automatically advances a Faction once. The answer states the ordinary public-offer fallback; it does not claim that reserved contracts are public or deny Shaddam his separate Leader option. Unasked reserved-contract details are not imported as extra question parts.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

observed.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.

grades.reason: All three spaces have their requested icons, costs, effects and Combat status, including Arrakeen's separate controller Solari.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.
grades.source_references: Supplements pp1–2; Main p10; FAQ p2 Maker hooks

observed.answer: Deep Desert uses Spice Trade access, costs 3 water, and offers either 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin also uses Spice Trade, costs 1 water, and offers either 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Both grant all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choosing worms; Hooks are retained, not spent.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms; FAQ Spies/Hooks

grades.reason: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin have the correct water costs and mutually exclusive base-spice/worm quantities; bonus spice remains collectible and Hooks are retained.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.

grades.reason: Both Sietch options share City access, two Fremen Influence and no resource cost; the separate effects are given and removing the Wall grants no troop.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access and costs 5 Solari each visit; it is not Combat. First visit: place Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits: gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.

grades.reason: High Council's first and later effects, five-Solari cost on each visit, ongoing Reveal Persuasion and noncombat status are correct.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster uses Landsraad access; it costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster, and 6 once anyone has one. Each player may do it once per game. Take the third Agent, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival getting its Swordmaster also lowers human cost to 6.

grades.reason: The eight-to-six cost change, once-per-player limit, same-round and permanent Agent availability, and Rival-triggered discount are all given.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence; it is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.

grades.reason: Imperial Privilege has Landsraad access, three-Solari entry and two Emperor Influence requirement, optional Intrigue exchange, other-Agent recall and card draw, with no automatic Emperor gain.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

observed.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence and costs 3 spice; it is not Combat. Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, not necessarily the Guild.

grades.reason: Shipping's Spice Trade access, Guild threshold, three-spice cost, five Solari and freely chosen Faction gain are correct.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

observed.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops; if you paid 2 Solari, also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is Combat; choose to pay 0 or 1 spice to gain respectively 2 or 4 Solari; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.

grades.reason: Gather Support's two troops and optional paid water and Refinery's two/four Solari plus controller benefit are distinguished with their correct Combat statuses.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

observed.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild icon, 5 spice cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen icon, 1 water cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop and optionally trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor icon, 4 spice cost, Combat no; gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four troops.

grades.reason: All three spaces have the correct costs, Influence and troop counts, additional effects and deployment permissions.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

observed.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad icon, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit icon, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild icon, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.

grades.reason: All three icons, costs and effects are given, including Assembly Hall's requirement that the Agent remain there during Reveal.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?
grades.expected: Each affected opponent moves Spy to empty observation post not connected to this turn Agent destination. Can play without enemy Spy there. Litany red box ignored during Reveal or with gained Agent icon when played normally as Agent card.
grades.source_references: FAQ pp2–3 False Orders/Litany Against Fear

observed.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as an Agent card.
observed.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear

grades.reason: False Orders moves affected Spies to legal empty nonconnected posts and remains playable without an opposing Spy there; both Litany red-box exceptions are correct.

grades.question: With Manipulate, may opponents acquire the removed card, may you acquire it by other means with the discount, and when does an unacquired card leave the game?
grades.expected: Opponents cannot acquire. You may use other means but 1-Persuasion discount does not apply. If not acquired by end of next Reveal turn, remove from game.

observed.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired at the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.

grades.reason: Opponents cannot acquire the removed card; the user can acquire by other means without discount, and expiry is the end of the next Reveal.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?
grades.expected: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.

observed.answer: Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside board, three Spies, and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal near the Rival and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it can win.

grades.reason: The full Rival setup, retained 2P Reshuffle and ability to trigger Endgame and win are given.

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5; p2 Swordmaster; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: When its total resources reach its printed Swordmaster value, spend exactly that amount and take its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count all Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water in supply, each one counting as one, including starting water. Mandatory spend order: Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers after paying the value. The Agent is immediately usable.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Swordmaster resource total and spending priority

grades.reason: The immediate printed-value threshold, one-per-resource counting, exact spending amount, mandatory type order, retained leftovers and immediate Agent availability are all given.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?
grades.expected: Each set 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigues or 3 water gives 1 VP whenever available. No mixed seven-resource VP purchase; mixed total only used for Swordmaster.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5 Buying Victory Points diagram

observed.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each exact set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards or 3 water for 1 VP. Mixed resource totals do not qualify; it cannot spend a mixed seven for VP.

grades.reason: The four homogeneous resource thresholds are exact and mixed-resource VP purchases are excluded.

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

observed.answer: Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP as a human does, but not the 4-Influence track bonus. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its Rival card’s Faction priority list.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Influence; resource gains

grades.reason: Least Influence and leftmost priority choose the Faction; Influence and Alliance VP apply but the four-Influence resource bonus does not, and numbered Hagal icons use printed priority positions.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.
grades.source_references: Supplements p4 Special Instructions; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: No. For a two-destination card, use only the condition-matching destination; if that destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card without using the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.

grades.reason: The condition-selected occupied destination cannot be replaced with the alternate; the two condition types are correctly identified.

grades.question: A Rival has no troops newly recruited by a card sending it to Combat. Can it deploy garrison troops? What if a Hagal card recruits at a noncombat space or has a conditional 2-Influence bonus not met?
grades.expected: Still deploy up to two available garrison troops at Combat. New troops at noncombat go garrison. Missing 2-Influence bonus does not block placement, just no bonus. Use only Hagal effects, not ordinary board effects.

observed.answer: Yes, at every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops, even if the card recruited none. At a noncombat space recruited troops go into its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent Agent placement; just omit that bonus.

grades.reason: A combat visit still deploys up to two garrison troops with no new recruits, noncombat recruits remain garrisoned, and failure of the conditional Influence bonus does not block placement.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: Unless specified, choose the first available Faction observation post in priority order. If all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third/final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes

grades.reason: Unrestricted placement follows Faction priority, full Faction posts give no placement, the final Spy triggers recall of the other two and Scheme, and the Rival uses neither voluntary recall ability.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.answer: If Scheme recruits before placement and the Rival visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those newly recruited troops too. If Place Spy finds no empty post of the required type, ignore the placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Spies and Schemes

grades.reason: Same-turn Scheme recruits are eligible for the ensuing Combat placement, and a failed Place Spy still leads to another Hagal reveal in that Agent turn.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?
grades.expected: Always take bonus spice. With Hooks and summonable Conflict summons one at Hagga/two Deep instead of base. Without Hooks or if protected, summons none and gains base spice (2/4). At Imperial Basin gains base1. Hagal wall removal requires Hooks.

observed.answer: The Rival always takes all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, it summons one/two worms instead of base spice; if it summons none, it takes base spice (2/4). Without Hooks, or if worms are prohibited by the Wall, it takes base spice. Hooks are not spent.

grades.reason: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice, chooses one/two worms with Hooks and a legal Conflict, and otherwise takes the two/four base spice.

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?
grades.expected: Start Combat in turn order, only with deployed unit: one Hagal card, bottom swords only added. Reshuffle and draw again on Reshuffle. Humans then Combat Intrigue before resolution. No unit no bonus.

observed.answer: At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.

grades.reason: Only a deployed Rival gets a Combat-start bottom-sword Hagal bonus, Reshuffle causes another reveal, and humans receive their Intrigue window afterward.

grades.question: Can a Rival gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and doubled rewards? How does it handle optional Conflict VP payments and contract rewards with CHOAM?
grades.expected: Normal control visit bonus and defensive supply troop; win card/match icons; sandworms double. Always buy optional Conflict VP if can pay resources or required Spy recall. Never contracts; each contract reward becomes 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

observed.answer: Yes: Rival gains control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and sandworm-doubled rewards normally. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

grades.reason: Normal control, defense, card/icon and doubled rewards apply; payable optional Conflict VP is taken and contracts are replaced by two Solari even with CHOAM.

grades.question: When during Reveal do you total, announce and set Combat strength, can you update it during the turn, and how is strength over 20 marked?
grades.expected: After Reveal Cards and before Clean Up, at any point while resolving effects; announce total, set marker and update as needed. Above20 flip +20 side and count again from beginning of track.

observed.answer: During Reveal effects, total/announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point, updating it as needed. If strength exceeds 20, flip marker to +20 side and start again from the beginning of track.

grades.reason: Strength can be totalled, announced, set and updated during Reveal resolution; over twenty uses the flipped +20 marker and a fresh count on the track.

grades.question: When is a Leader’s Signet Ring ability activated, does merely revealing Signet Ring activate it, and can card text override normal game rules?
grades.expected: Activated when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not when merely revealing. Left Leader ability used as described. Cards of any type can override normal rules.

observed.answer: A human Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when revealed. Card text may override usual game rules.

grades.reason: Human Signet activation is an Agent-turn play rather than mere Reveal, and card text can override ordinary rules.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

Moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard at Clean Up does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.

grades.reason: Upward passage through two counts and may recur after losing Influence, downward passage does not, and Clean Up is not a hand discard for Spacing Guild's Favor.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade Agent icon: draw one card and resolve a contract icon; it does not automatically gain Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor Agent icon: gain one Emperor Influence and resolve a contract icon. Without CHOAM each contract icon gives 2 Solari. With CHOAM, take an available public face-up contract into your supply and refill from the bank if possible; the icon gives 2 Solari if no such contract remains. For another human, Shaddam's unacquired set-aside Sardaukar contracts are unavailable and do not prevent this fallback when the public supply is empty. Shaddam's reserved-contract acquisition option remains governed by his Leader and the FAQ.
grades.source_references: See benchmark-v17/source-reference-appendix.json: original main PDF pp16,20, Uprising Board Space Guide, original Shaddam Leader and official FAQ p3, exact named-file/hash locators.

The answer states the ordinary public-offer fallback; it does not claim that reserved contracts are public or deny Shaddam his separate Leader option. grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

observed.answer: Arrakeen: City, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card, controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw 1 card. Research Station: City, 2 water, Combat yes; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.

grades.reason: All three spaces have their requested icons, costs, effects and Combat status, including Arrakeen's separate controller Solari.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.
grades.source_references: Supplements pp1–2; Main p10; FAQ p2 Maker hooks

Both also grant all bonus spice even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent; effects specifying Hooks require having the token.

grades.reason: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin have the correct water costs and mutually exclusive base-spice/worm quantities; bonus spice remains collectible and Hooks are retained.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource cost. Option 1: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit 1 troop, gain 1 water. Option 2: gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall; it gives no troop.

grades.reason: Both Sietch options share City access, two Fremen Influence and no resource cost; the separate effects are given and removing the Wall grants no troop.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council is Landsraad, no Combat, costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit puts your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn thereafter. Later visits grant 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit 3 troops.

grades.reason: High Council's first and later effects, five-Solari cost on each visit, ongoing Reveal Persuasion and noncombat status are correct.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one, then 6; each player may gain it only once. Take the third Agent, available this round and for the rest of the game. Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.

grades.reason: The eight-to-six cost change, once-per-player limit, same-round and permanent Agent availability, and Rival-triggered discount are all given.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad, costs 3 Solari, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It gives no automatic Emperor Influence.

grades.reason: Imperial Privilege has Landsraad access, three-Solari entry and two Emperor Influence requirement, optional Intrigue exchange, other-Agent recall and card draw, with no automatic Emperor gain.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

observed.answer: Shipping is Spice Trade, requires 2+ Guild Influence and costs 3 spice; it gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction. The free-choice Influence need not be Guild. It is not a Combat space.

grades.reason: Shipping's Spice Trade access, Guild threshold, three-spice cost, five Solari and freely chosen Faction gain are correct.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

observed.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, non-Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1; controller separately gains 1 Solari.

grades.reason: Gather Support's two troops and optional paid water and Refinery's two/four Solari plus controller benefit are distinguished with their correct Combat statuses.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits 1 troop, may trash a card; Combat yes. grades.reason: All three spaces have the correct costs, Influence and troop counts, additional effects and deployment permissions.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, non-Combat; gain 1 BG Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, non-Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.

grades.reason: All three icons, costs and effects are given, including Assembly Hall's requirement that the Agent remain there during Reveal.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?

Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
observed.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

grades.reason: False Orders moves affected Spies to legal empty nonconnected posts and remains playable without an opposing Spy there; both Litany red-box exceptions are correct.

grades.question: With Manipulate, may opponents acquire the removed card, may you acquire it by other means with the discount, and when does an unacquired card leave the game?
grades.expected: Opponents cannot acquire. You may use other means but 1-Persuasion discount does not apply. If not acquired by end of next Reveal turn, remove from game.

observed.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it remains unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.

grades.reason: Opponents cannot acquire the removed card; the user can acquire by other means without discount, and expiry is the end of the next Reveal.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?

grades.reason: The requested Rival component setup omits its four Faction Influence cubes at the bottoms of the tracks. All other requested starting components/resources, retained Reshuffle and scoring threat are answered correctly.

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5; p2 Swordmaster; FAQ p3 Rivals

grades.reason: The immediate printed-value threshold, one-per-resource counting, exact spending amount, mandatory type order, retained leftovers and immediate Agent availability are all given.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?
grades.expected: Each set 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigues or 3 water gives 1 VP whenever available. No mixed seven-resource VP purchase; mixed total only used for Swordmaster.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5 Buying Victory Points diagram

observed.answer: After Swordmaster, spend 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP per set. Mixed totals do not qualify.

grades.reason: The four homogeneous resource thresholds are exact and mixed-resource VP purchases are excluded.

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

Rival gains/losses VP at 2 Influence and gains/loses Alliance VP like a human, but does not receive 4-Influence track bonuses. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in the Rival card’s Faction priority list.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster; Agent turns.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.

grades.reason: The condition-selected occupied destination cannot be replaced with the alternate; the two condition types are correctly identified.

grades.question: A Rival has no troops newly recruited by a card sending it to Combat. Can it deploy garrison troops? What if a Hagal card recruits at a noncombat space or has a conditional 2-Influence bonus not met?
grades.expected: Still deploy up to two available garrison troops at Combat. New troops at noncombat go garrison. Missing 2-Influence bonus does not block placement, just no bonus. Use only Hagal effects, not ordinary board effects.

grades.reason: A combat visit still deploys up to two garrison troops with no new recruits, noncombat recruits remain garrisoned, and failure of the conditional Influence bonus does not block placement.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

grades.reason: Unrestricted placement follows Faction priority, full Faction posts give no placement, the final Spy triggers recall of the other two and Scheme, and the Rival uses neither voluntary recall ability.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.answer: Scheme-recruited troops can deploy if the Rival visits a Combat space that same turn. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, but Rival immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues because it has not placed an Agent.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

grades.reason: Same-turn Scheme recruits are eligible for the ensuing Combat placement, and a failed Place Spy still leads to another Hagal reveal in that Agent turn. “Can deploy” is accepted as contextual eligibility for these newly recruited troops, with no affirmative option to withhold an otherwise mandatory Rival deployment asserted.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?
grades.expected: Always take bonus spice. With Hooks and summonable Conflict summons one at Hagga/two Deep instead of base. Without Hooks or if protected, summons none and gains base spice (2/4). At Imperial Basin gains base1. Hagal wall removal requires Hooks.

observed.answer: At Hagga/Deep Desert, Rival collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict permitting worms, summon one at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice; if it summons none, take base spice (2/4). Thus without Hooks, or at protected Conflict, take base spice.

grades.reason: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice, chooses one/two worms with Hooks and a legal Conflict, and otherwise takes the two/four base spice.

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?
grades.expected: Start Combat in turn order, only with deployed unit: one Hagal card, bottom swords only added. Reshuffle and draw again on Reshuffle. Humans then Combat Intrigue before resolution. No unit no bonus.

observed.answer: At Combat start, if Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords; on Reshuffle reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then get their normal Combat Intrigue window. Unit-free Rival receives no bonus.

grades.reason: Only a deployed Rival gets a Combat-start bottom-sword Hagal bonus, Reshuffle causes another reveal, and humans receive their Intrigue window afterward.

grades.question: Can a Rival gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and doubled rewards? How does it handle optional Conflict VP payments and contract rewards with CHOAM?
grades.expected: Normal control visit bonus and defensive supply troop; win card/match icons; sandworms double. Always buy optional Conflict VP if can pay resources or required Spy recall. Never contracts; each contract reward becomes 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

observed.answer: Yes: Rival gets control and defensive troop bonuses, battle-icon VP, and doubles rewards with worms; it wins cards normally. Always take optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

grades.reason: Normal control, defense, card/icon and doubled rewards apply; payable optional Conflict VP is taken and contracts are replaced by two Solari even with CHOAM.

grades.question: When during Reveal do you total, announce and set Combat strength, can you update it during the turn, and how is strength over 20 marked?
grades.expected: After Reveal Cards and before Clean Up, at any point while resolving effects; announce total, set marker and update as needed. Above20 flip +20 side and count again from beginning of track.

grades.reason: Strength can be totalled, announced, set and updated during Reveal resolution; over twenty uses the flipped +20 marker and a fresh count on the track.

grades.question: When is a Leader’s Signet Ring ability activated, does merely revealing Signet Ring activate it, and can card text override normal game rules?
grades.expected: Activated when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not when merely revealing. Left Leader ability used as described. Cards of any type can override normal rules.

grades.reason: Human Signet activation is an Agent-turn play rather than mere Reveal, and card text can override ordinary rules.

grades.question: How is a Recall Spy icon on a card resolved, where does the Spy go, and is it automatically the same as Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: Return one of own Spies from observation post to supply, usually a cost for card effect. Card recall distinct from the two voluntary recalls for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; it does not automatically give either benefit.

grades.reason: The icon recalls one's Spy from its post to supply, usually as a cost, and does not independently confer Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.

grades.question: What does the “trash an Intrigue” icon allow you to choose, as opposed to an ordinary discard-a-card instruction?
grades.expected: Trash an Intrigue of choice from own hand. Ordinary discard chooses a non-Intrigue from hand unless explicitly specified.

grades.question: A Conflict reward grants one Influence of your choice and is doubled by your sandworm. May the two gains go to different Factions? Contrast a single effect that grants two Influence.
grades.expected: Yes. Sandworm doubling of a one-Influence reward gives two separate gains, which may use the same Faction or two different Factions. A single two-Influence effect instead chooses just one Faction and cannot be split.
grades.source_references: Main PDF p14 Sandworm Reward Doubling example and p20 Influence icons / extraction 778–791,1123–1126

observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Special Rules: Influence.

grades.reason: A doubled one-Influence reward permits separate Faction choices, whereas a single two-Influence effect is indivisible.

grades.question: A House Hagal card shows a Signet Ring effect for the two-player Rival. Which ability is resolved, and does the Rival need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn to trigger it?
grades.expected: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card as the Hagal effect. No human deck Signet Ring card or Reveal turn is involved; Rival never Reveals.

observed.answer: Resolve the Rival card’s printed Signet Ring ability. Do not substitute Scheme. It is triggered by the Hagal Signet Ring effect; no human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn is involved.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme.

grades.reason: Hagal's Signet icon invokes the selected Rival's Signet ability rather than Scheme, without a human Signet card or Reveal turn.

grades.question: For a two-player Rival, what do House Hagal Maker Hooks and Shield Wall removal icons do if it already has Hooks, lacks Hooks, or the wall is already gone?

observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Hooks and Wall icons.

grades.reason: Hooks acquisition does not duplicate an owned token; Rival Wall removal requires its Hooks and an existing Wall, with both failure cases correctly handled.

grades.question: For Secrets, state its Agent icon, entry cost, Combat status and all effects, including which Intrigues come from the deck and which come from opponents.
grades.expected: Bene Gesserit, no cost, not Combat. Gain one BG Influence and draw one Intrigue from deck. Each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one randomly selected Intrigue; below four gives none.
grades.source_references: Supplements PDF p2 Secrets; Main p7 Intrigue and p20 Steal Intrigue

observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Intrigue cards.
